lessons.title: Soft Sounds of c and g, and Consonant Clusters
lessons.notes_html:
Soft Sound of 'c'

The letter c has a soft sound like s in these words: city, pencil, face. More words with the soft sound of c: fence, dice, case, cycle, mice.

Soft Sound of 'g'

The letter g has a soft sound like j in these words: giant, orange, pigeon. More words with the soft sound of g: germ, page, German, ginger.

Consonant Clusters

A consonant cluster is two consonants together in a word.

  • sh — shop, fish.
  • st — star, stone.

Poem and Tongue Twister

The poem 'If You're Happy' is recited with actions. Tongue twister: She sells sea shells by the seashore.

mcqs.q: Which word has the soft sound of 'c', like the sound of 's'?
mcqs.why: In 'city' the letter c is soft and sounds like s. In cat, cup and cake, the c has its hard sound.

mcqs.q: Which of these words also has the soft sound of 'c'?
mcqs.why: The word 'face' has the soft c sound, like s. The words dog, sun and bag have no letter c at all.

mcqs.q: The letter 'g' has a soft sound, like 'j', in which word?
mcqs.why: In 'giant' the g is soft and sounds like j. In goat, gum and gate, the g keeps its hard sound.

mcqs.q: Which word has the soft sound of 'g'?
mcqs.why: The word 'orange' ends with a soft g that sounds like j, just like the g in giant and pigeon.

mcqs.q: What is a consonant cluster?
options: A vowel sound in a word
Two consonants together in a word
A silent letter in a word
mcqs.why: A consonant cluster is two consonants together in a word, such as 'st' in star or 'sh' in shop.

mcqs.q: Which pair of words shows the cluster 'sh'?
mcqs.why: Shop begins with sh and fish ends with sh. Star and stone show the other cluster, st, instead.

mcqs.q: Which pair of words shows the cluster 'st'?
mcqs.why: Star and stone both begin with the consonant cluster st. All the other pairs show the cluster sh.

mcqs.q: Which of these words has the soft sound of 'c'?
mcqs.why: In 'dice' the c is soft and sounds like s. In corn, cold and cup, the c has its hard k sound.

mcqs.q: Which word does NOT have the soft sound of 'g'?
mcqs.why: In 'goat' the g is hard. Germ, page and ginger all have the soft g sound, which is like j.

mcqs.q: The tongue twister in this lesson is about:
mcqs.why: The tongue twister is 'She sells sea shells by the seashore', which gives practice of the sh and s sounds.

lessons.title: Respect Symbols and Class Rules
lessons.notes_html:
Respect Symbols

  • Looking Eyes — look towards the person talking to you.
  • Listening Ears — listen with full attention.
  • Helping Hands — join hands to help.
  • Walking Feet — walk with the friend to help.
  • Speaking Nicely — an educated person always speaks nicely.

Rules of the Classroom

  • Use manners and be polite.
  • Help others.
  • Be kind to others.
  • Be ready to learn everyday.
  • Look after your school.
  • Follow instructions.

Model: The class rule I like the most is 'Help others' because helping others makes everyone happy.

mcqs.q: What do 'Looking Eyes' ask us to do?
options: Look towards the person talking to us
mcqs.why: Looking Eyes mean we look towards the person who is talking to us, to show respect and attention.

mcqs.q: 'Listening Ears' means we should:
mcqs.why: Listening Ears remind us to listen with full attention when someone is speaking to us.

mcqs.q: What do 'Helping Hands' ask us to do?
mcqs.why: Helping Hands mean we join hands to help others, which is one of the respect symbols of the class.

mcqs.q: 'Walking Feet' means we should:
options: walk with the friend to help
mcqs.why: Walking Feet mean we walk with a friend to help him or her, instead of leaving the friend alone.

mcqs.q: An educated person always:
mcqs.why: Speaking nicely is a sign of an educated person, so we should always speak nicely with everyone.

mcqs.q: Which one is a rule of the classroom?
mcqs.why: Helping others is one of the classroom rules, along with being kind and being ready to learn.

mcqs.q: Which of these is NOT a classroom rule?
mcqs.why: Shouting and running in class breaks the rules. The real rules are to be kind, follow instructions and look after the school.

mcqs.q: According to the class rules, we should look after:
mcqs.why: One of the classroom rules is 'Look after your school', so we keep our school clean and safe.

mcqs.q: Which class rule did the writer like the most?
mcqs.why: The writer liked 'Help others' the most because helping others makes everyone happy.

mcqs.q: The classroom rules ask us to use manners and be:
mcqs.why: The first classroom rule is to use manners and be polite with teachers and classmates.

lessons.title: Comprehension: The First Day of a New Class
lessons.notes_html:
Key Facts

  • Meeting old friends, meeting the new teacher and seeing the new classroom make a student happy on the first day of a new class.
  • It is important to listen to our teachers because teachers teach us new things and guide us.
  • We keep our class clean by throwing rubbish in the dustbin and keeping our desk tidy.
  • Rules like 'listen with full attention', 'speak nicely' and 'be ready to learn everyday' help us to learn English.
  • Two important rules for the classroom: (1) Help others. (2) Look after your school.

mcqs.q: What makes a student happy on the first day of a new class?
mcqs.why: Meeting old friends, meeting the new teacher and seeing the new classroom make a student happy on the first day.

mcqs.q: Why is it important to listen to our teachers?
options: Teachers teach us new things and guide us
mcqs.why: We listen to our teachers because they teach us new things and guide us in the right way.

mcqs.q: How do we keep our class clean?
options: By throwing rubbish on the floor
By throwing rubbish in the dustbin and keeping our desk tidy
By leaving books on the floor
mcqs.why: We keep our class clean by throwing rubbish in the dustbin and keeping our desk tidy.

mcqs.q: Which rule helps us to learn English?
mcqs.why: Rules like 'listen with full attention', 'speak nicely' and 'be ready to learn everyday' help us to learn English.

mcqs.q: Which pair names two important rules for the classroom?
options: Help others; look after your school
Sleep in class; eat in class
mcqs.why: The two important rules are: (1) Help others, and (2) Look after your school.

mcqs.q: On the first day, seeing the new ______ also makes a student happy.
mcqs.why: Seeing the new classroom, along with meeting old friends and the new teacher, makes a student happy.

mcqs.q: We keep our desk:
mcqs.why: Keeping our desk tidy is one way we keep our class clean, together with using the dustbin.

mcqs.q: Teachers teach us new things and ______ us.
mcqs.why: Teachers teach us new things and guide us, which is why listening to them is important.

mcqs.q: Where should we throw rubbish in the classroom?
mcqs.why: Rubbish always goes in the dustbin; that is how we keep our class clean.

mcqs.q: On the first day of a new class, we also meet:
mcqs.why: Meeting the new teacher is one of the things that make a student happy on the first day.

lessons.title: Syllables and Alphabetical Order
lessons.notes_html:
Syllables

A syllable is one beat of sound in a word.

  • learn = learn (1)
  • through = through (1)
  • activity = ac-ti-vi-ty (4)
  • poem = po-em (2)
  • fun = fun (1)
  • poster = pos-ter (2)

Alphabetical Order

activity, fun, learn, poem, poster, through.

mcqs.q: What is a syllable?
options: One beat of sound in a word
The last letter of a word
mcqs.why: A syllable is one beat of sound in a word, like the four beats in ac-ti-vi-ty.

mcqs.q: How many syllables are there in 'activity'?
mcqs.why: Activity is divided as ac-ti-vi-ty, which makes four syllables, or four beats of sound.

mcqs.q: How many syllables are there in 'poem'?
mcqs.why: Poem is divided as po-em, so it has two syllables.

mcqs.q: How many syllables are there in 'poster'?
mcqs.why: Poster is divided as pos-ter, so it has two syllables.

mcqs.q: Which word has only ONE syllable?
mcqs.why: Learn is a single beat of sound, so it has one syllable. Poster and poem have two, and activity has four.

mcqs.q: Which word has FOUR syllables?
mcqs.why: Activity (ac-ti-vi-ty) is the only word here with four syllables; fun, through and learn each have one.

mcqs.q: In alphabetical order, which word comes FIRST?
mcqs.why: Alphabetical order begins with the letter a, so 'activity' comes first in the list.

mcqs.q: In alphabetical order, which word comes LAST?
mcqs.why: The full order is activity, fun, learn, poem, poster, through — so 'through' comes last.

mcqs.q: Which list is in correct alphabetical order?
options: fun, activity, learn, poem, poster, through
activity, fun, learn, poem, poster, through
through, poster, poem, learn, fun, activity
activity, learn, fun, poem, through, poster
mcqs.why: Words are arranged by their first letters: a, f, l, p, p, t — giving activity, fun, learn, poem, poster, through.

mcqs.q: 'Through' has how many syllables?
mcqs.why: Through is spoken as one beat of sound, so it has only one syllable, like learn and fun.

lessons.title: Grammar: Proper and Common Nouns, Opposites and Sentences
lessons.notes_html:
Proper and Common Nouns

A proper noun is the special name of a person, place or thing. A common noun is a general naming word.

  • 'Pakistan is my country' — proper noun: Pakistan; common noun: country.
  • 'My sister's name is Maryam' — proper noun: Maryam; common nouns: sister, name.
  • 'I like chocolate ice-cream' — common nouns: chocolate, ice-cream.
  • Five proper nouns: Ali, Lahore, Pakistan, Ravi, Maryam.
  • Five common nouns: boy, book, school, teacher, bag.

Opposites

  • good — bad
  • clean — dirty
  • kind — unkind
  • polite — rude
  • happy — sad
  • healthy — unhealthy

Model Sentences

  • I learn English in my classroom.
  • She is a good girl.
  • Keep your classroom clean.
  • English is easy to learn.
  • Our classroom is big.
  • The poster is on the wall.

mcqs.q: What is a proper noun?
options: The special name of a person, place or thing
mcqs.why: A proper noun is the special name of a person, place or thing, like Ali, Lahore or Pakistan.

mcqs.q: What is a common noun?
options: The name of one special person
A word with a capital letter
mcqs.why: A common noun is a general naming word, like boy, book, school, teacher or bag.

mcqs.q: In 'Pakistan is my country', the proper noun is:
mcqs.why: Pakistan is the special name of a country, so it is the proper noun; 'country' is the common noun.

mcqs.q: In 'Pakistan is my country', the common noun is:
mcqs.why: The word 'country' is a general naming word, so it is a common noun, while Pakistan is a proper noun.

mcqs.q: In 'My sister's name is Maryam', which word is a proper noun?
mcqs.why: Maryam is the special name of a person, so it is a proper noun; sister and name are common nouns.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a common noun?
mcqs.why: Book is a general naming word, so it is a common noun. Ali, Lahore and Ravi are special names, so they are proper nouns.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a proper noun?
mcqs.why: Maryam is the special name of a person, so it is a proper noun. Boy, school and teacher are common nouns.

mcqs.q: What is the opposite of 'good'?
mcqs.why: The opposite of good is bad, just as the opposite of clean is dirty and of happy is sad.

mcqs.q: What is the opposite of 'polite'?
mcqs.why: The opposite of polite is rude. A polite person speaks nicely, but a rude person does not.

mcqs.q: What is the opposite of 'kind'?
mcqs.why: The opposite of kind is unkind; adding 'un' at the start makes the opposite, like unhealthy from healthy.

lessons.title: Writing: Syllables, Punctuation and 'My Classroom'
lessons.notes_html:
Dividing Words into Syllables

  • classroom = class-room (2)
  • consonants = con-so-nants (3)
  • clusters = clus-ters (2)
  • playground = play-ground (2)
  • correct = cor-rect (2)
  • happy = hap-py (2)

Punctuation and Capital Letters

Hello everyone! Today is my first day in Class III. I am very happy. All my friends are also very happy.

Model Writing: My Classroom

My classroom is big and clean. There are thirty students in my class. Our English teacher is kind. We have chairs, tables and a whiteboard in our classroom. We read, write and play fun games in our classroom. I love my classroom very much.

mcqs.q: How many syllables are there in 'classroom'?
mcqs.why: Classroom is divided as class-room, which gives two syllables.

mcqs.q: How many syllables are there in 'consonants'?
mcqs.why: Consonants is divided as con-so-nants, which gives three syllables.

mcqs.q: Which word has THREE syllables?
mcqs.why: Consonants (con-so-nants) has three syllables; happy, correct and clusters each have two.

mcqs.q: 'Playground' is divided into syllables as:
mcqs.why: Playground divides as play-ground, two syllables, just like class-room.

mcqs.q: How many syllables are there in 'happy'?
mcqs.why: Happy is divided as hap-py, so it has two syllables.

mcqs.q: According to the model writing, how many students are there in the class?
mcqs.why: The model paragraph 'My Classroom' says: 'There are thirty students in my class.'

mcqs.q: What do we have in the classroom, besides chairs and tables?
mcqs.why: The model writing says: 'We have chairs, tables and a whiteboard in our classroom.'

mcqs.q: How is the English teacher described in 'My Classroom'?
mcqs.why: The paragraph says 'Our English teacher is kind', and the writer loves the classroom very much.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is written with correct capital letters and punctuation?
options: hello everyone! today is my first day in class III.
Hello everyone! Today is my first day in Class III.
Hello everyone today is my first day in Class III
hello Everyone! Today is my first day in class iii.
mcqs.why: A sentence begins with a capital letter, and names like Class III also take capitals; the second sentence is fully correct.

mcqs.q: In the model writing, what do we do in the classroom?
options: Read, write and play fun games
mcqs.why: The paragraph says: 'We read, write and play fun games in our classroom.'

lessons.title: Long and Short Vowel Sounds
lessons.notes_html:
Long and Short Vowels

  • a — hat (short), hard (long).
  • e — bed (short), bee (long).
  • i — ink (short), ice (long).
  • o — box (short), boat (long).
  • u — cut (short), cute (long).

Reading practice words: bell, red, heat, fell, seat, bin, sit, lid, kit, bit.

Sight Words

golden, shine, earth, good-bye.

Tongue Twister

How much wood would a woodchuck chuck, if the woodchuck could chuck wood?

mcqs.q: Which word has the SHORT sound of 'a'?
mcqs.why: The a in 'hat' is short, while the a in 'hard' is long.

mcqs.q: Which word has the LONG sound of 'e'?
mcqs.why: The e in 'bee' is long, while bed, bell and red all have the short e sound.

mcqs.q: Which pair shows short and long sounds of 'i'?
mcqs.why: Ink has the short i sound and ice has the long i sound, so 'ink — ice' is the correct pair.

mcqs.q: Which word has the LONG sound of 'o'?
mcqs.why: The o in 'boat' is long, while box, pot and top have the short o sound.

mcqs.q: Which word has the SHORT sound of 'u'?
mcqs.why: The u in 'cut' is short, while the u in cute, tube and mule is long.

mcqs.q: Which of these reading words has the short 'e' sound?
mcqs.why: Fell has the short e sound, like bell and red. Heat and seat have the long e sound.

mcqs.q: Which word has the long 'i' sound?
mcqs.why: Ice begins with the long i sound. Ink, sit and bin all have the short i sound.

mcqs.q: Which is a sight word from this lesson?
mcqs.why: The sight words of this lesson are golden, shine, earth and good-bye; 'golden' is one of them.

mcqs.q: The tongue twister of this lesson is about a:
mcqs.why: The tongue twister asks: 'How much wood would a woodchuck chuck, if the woodchuck could chuck wood?'

mcqs.q: Which pair shows short and long sounds of 'a'?
mcqs.why: Hat has the short a sound and hard has the long a sound, so 'hat — hard' is the correct pair.

lessons.title: The Poem: Golden Sun
lessons.notes_html:
About the Poem

The poem 'Golden Sun' is about the sun and its blessings. The colour golden is used in the title because the sun looks golden when it shines.

Key Facts

  • Sunlight is a blessing because it gives us light and warmth and helps plants grow.
  • The poet loves the sun and feels happy when it shines.

Comparing 'Moon' and 'Golden Sun'

The sun shines in the day and looks golden, while the moon shines at night and looks silvery. Both give light to us.

mcqs.q: What is the poem 'Golden Sun' about?
mcqs.why: The poem 'Golden Sun' is about the sun and its blessings for us.

mcqs.q: Why is the colour golden used in the title of the poem?
options: The sun looks golden when it shines
The sky is golden at night
mcqs.why: The colour golden is used in the title because the sun looks golden when it shines.

mcqs.q: Why is sunlight a blessing for us?
options: It gives us light and warmth and helps plants grow
mcqs.why: Sunlight is a blessing because it gives us light and warmth and helps plants grow.

mcqs.q: How does the poet feel when the sun shines?
mcqs.why: The poet loves the sun and feels happy when it shines.

mcqs.q: When does the sun shine?
mcqs.why: The sun shines in the day and looks golden, while the moon shines at night and looks silvery.

mcqs.q: The moon looks:
mcqs.why: The moon shines at night and looks silvery, while the sun shines in the day and looks golden.

mcqs.q: What do the sun and the moon both give us?
mcqs.why: Both the sun and the moon give light to us — the sun in the day and the moon at night.

mcqs.q: Sunlight helps ______ to grow.
mcqs.why: Sunlight gives us light and warmth and helps plants grow, so it is a blessing of nature.

mcqs.q: Who loves the sun in the poem?
mcqs.why: The poet loves the sun and feels happy when it shines, and writes about its blessings.

mcqs.q: The sun looks golden when it:
mcqs.why: The sun looks golden when it shines, and that is why the poem is named 'Golden Sun'.

lessons.title: Syllables, Spellings and Anagrams
lessons.notes_html:
Syllables

  • great = great (1)
  • glorious = glo-ri-ous (3)
  • magic = ma-gic (2)
  • whole = whole (1)

Correct Spellings

EARTH, MAGIC, ENERGY, SHINE, DEPEND, HEALTH, FLOWER, WELCOME, WHOLE.

Anagrams

An anagram is a new word made by rearranging the letters of a word.

  • ear — era
  • act — cat
  • pat — tap
  • dam — mad
  • mug — gum
  • now — won

mcqs.q: How many syllables are there in 'glorious'?
mcqs.why: Glorious is divided as glo-ri-ous, which gives three syllables.

mcqs.q: How many syllables are there in 'magic'?
mcqs.why: Magic is divided as ma-gic, which gives two syllables.

mcqs.q: What is an anagram?
options: A new word made by rearranging the letters of a word
mcqs.why: An anagram is a new word made by rearranging the letters of a word, like cat from act.

mcqs.q: What is the anagram of 'ear'?
mcqs.why: Rearranging the letters of 'ear' gives 'era', so era is the anagram of ear.

mcqs.q: What is the anagram of 'act'?
mcqs.why: The letters a, c, t of 'act' can be rearranged to make 'cat', so cat is the anagram of act.

mcqs.q: What is the anagram of 'now'?
mcqs.why: Rearranging the letters of 'now' gives 'won', so won is the anagram of now.

mcqs.q: What is the anagram of 'pat'?
mcqs.why: The letters of 'pat' rearranged make 'tap', so tap is the anagram of pat.

mcqs.q: Which spelling is correct?
mcqs.why: The correct spelling is EARTH, like the other lesson words MAGIC, ENERGY and SHINE.

mcqs.q: How many syllables are there in 'great'?
mcqs.why: Great is spoken as one beat of sound, so it has only one syllable, like 'whole'.

mcqs.q: What is the anagram of 'mug'?
mcqs.why: Rearranging the letters of 'mug' gives 'gum', so gum is the anagram of mug.

lessons.title: Grammar: Conjunctions, and Subject and Verb
lessons.notes_html:
Conjunctions

A conjunction joins words or sentences: and, or, because, but.

  • He and his brother went to watch the cricket match.
  • Do you want to buy a shirt or a pair of shoes?
  • We believe in him because he is honest.
  • I wanted to watch a movie but watched a match.

Subject and Verb

  • 'She works hard' — subject: She; verb: works.
  • 'The teacher asks a question' — subject: The teacher; verb: asks.
  • 'My brother plays cricket' — subject: My brother; verb: plays.
  • 'She is my class teacher' — subject: She; verb: is.

mcqs.q: What does a conjunction do?
mcqs.why: A conjunction joins words or sentences; the joining words are and, or, because and but.

mcqs.q: Which word is a conjunction?
mcqs.why: Because is a conjunction; we use it in 'We believe in him because he is honest.'

mcqs.q: In 'He and his brother went to watch the cricket match', the conjunction is:
mcqs.why: The word 'and' joins 'He' with 'his brother', so 'and' is the conjunction in this sentence.

mcqs.q: Which conjunction completes: 'Do you want to buy a shirt ______ a pair of shoes?'
mcqs.why: The sentence offers a choice between a shirt and shoes, so the conjunction 'or' is used.

mcqs.q: In 'She works hard', the subject is:
mcqs.why: In 'She works hard', 'She' is the subject and 'works' is the verb.

mcqs.q: In 'The teacher asks a question', the verb is:
mcqs.why: In this sentence 'The teacher' is the subject and 'asks' is the verb, the action word.

mcqs.q: In 'My brother plays cricket', the subject is:
mcqs.why: The subject is 'My brother' — the one who does the action — and 'plays' is the verb.

mcqs.q: Which conjunction shows a reason in 'We believe in him ______ he is honest'?
mcqs.why: Because gives the reason: we believe in him because he is honest.

mcqs.q: In 'She is my class teacher', the verb is:
mcqs.why: In 'She is my class teacher', 'She' is the subject and 'is' is the verb.

mcqs.q: Which sentence uses 'but' correctly?
options: I wanted to watch a movie but watched a match.
I wanted to watch a movie because watched a match.
I wanted to watch a movie or watched a match.
I wanted to watch a movie and watched a match.
mcqs.why: But joins two different ideas: wanting to watch a movie but watching a match instead.

lessons.title: Writing: Numbers in Words, a Paragraph and a Comic Story
lessons.notes_html:
Numbers 50 to 100 in Words

50 Fifty, 51 Fifty One, 52 Fifty Two, 53 Fifty Three, 54 Fifty Four, 55 Fifty Five, 56 Fifty Six, 57 Fifty Seven, 58 Fifty Eight, 59 Fifty Nine, 60 Sixty, 61 Sixty One, 62 Sixty Two, 63 Sixty Three, 64 Sixty Four, 65 Sixty Five, 66 Sixty Six, 67 Sixty Seven, 68 Sixty Eight, 69 Sixty Nine, 70 Seventy, 71 Seventy One, 72 Seventy Two, 73 Seventy Three, 74 Seventy Four, 75 Seventy Five, 76 Seventy Six, 77 Seventy Seven, 78 Seventy Eight, 79 Seventy Nine, 80 Eighty, 81 Eighty One, 82 Eighty Two, 83 Eighty Three, 84 Eighty Four, 85 Eighty Five, 86 Eighty Six, 87 Eighty Seven, 88 Eighty Eight, 89 Eighty Nine, 90 Ninety, 91 Ninety One, 92 Ninety Two, 93 Ninety Three, 94 Ninety Four, 95 Ninety Five, 96 Ninety Six, 97 Ninety Seven, 98 Ninety Eight, 99 Ninety Nine, 100 Hundred.

Model Paragraph: Neelum Valley

Neelum is a beautiful valley. There are almost 370 small and large villages. Nearly 2000 people live there. It is named after the Neelum for its clean water. The whole valley is full of beautiful scenery.

Comic Strip Story: Benny and Spike

Benny shares his berries with Spike. Spike thinks Benny is learning to be nice. Then Spike realises Benny is the one who took his berries.

mcqs.q: How is 60 written in words?
mcqs.why: The number 60 is written as 'Sixty'; sixteen is 16 and six hundred is 600.

mcqs.q: How is 75 written in words?
mcqs.why: 75 is written as 'Seventy Five' — seventy for the tens and five for the ones.

mcqs.q: How is 100 written in words?
mcqs.why: The number 100 is written as 'Hundred' in the numbers list of this lesson.

mcqs.q: How is 52 written in words?
mcqs.why: 52 is written as 'Fifty Two' — fifty for the tens and two for the ones.

mcqs.q: How is 99 written in words?
mcqs.why: 99 is written as 'Ninety Nine' — ninety for the tens and nine for the ones.

mcqs.q: About how many villages are there in Neelum Valley?
mcqs.why: The paragraph says there are almost 370 small and large villages in Neelum Valley.

mcqs.q: Nearly how many people live in Neelum Valley?
mcqs.why: The paragraph says nearly 2000 people live in Neelum Valley.

mcqs.q: Why is the valley named Neelum?
mcqs.why: The valley is named after the Neelum for its clean water, and it is full of beautiful scenery.

mcqs.q: In the comic story, what does Benny share with Spike?
mcqs.why: In the comic strip story, Benny shares his berries with Spike, and Spike thinks Benny is learning to be nice.

mcqs.q: At the end of the comic story, Spike realises that:
options: Benny is the one who took his berries
mcqs.why: Spike finally realises that Benny is the one who took his berries in the first place.

lessons.title: Exclamations and Introducing Yourself
lessons.notes_html:
Exclamations

An exclamation shows a strong feeling like sorrow, pain or joy.

  • Bano's toy has been broken — Alas!
  • Ali fell from the cycle and hurt his ankle — Oh!
  • Pakistan has won the cricket match against England — Hurrah!

Introducing Yourself

When you introduce yourself, tell: your name; the names of your family members; your favourite book and food; your pet, toy or game; and your family rules.

Poem and Sight Words

The poem 'Finger Family' is sung with actions. Sight words: happy, home, house, skill.

mcqs.q: What does an exclamation show?
options: A strong feeling like sorrow, pain or joy
mcqs.why: An exclamation shows a strong feeling like sorrow, pain or joy, such as Alas!, Oh! or Hurrah!

mcqs.q: Bano's toy has been broken. Which exclamation fits?
mcqs.why: A broken toy is a sad thing, so the exclamation of sorrow 'Alas!' fits here.

mcqs.q: Ali fell from the cycle and hurt his ankle. Which exclamation fits?
mcqs.why: Ali is in pain because he hurt his ankle, so the exclamation 'Oh!' shows his pain.

mcqs.q: Pakistan has won the cricket match against England. Which exclamation fits?
mcqs.why: Winning a match is a happy moment, so the exclamation of joy 'Hurrah!' fits here.

mcqs.q: When you introduce yourself, you should tell:
options: your name, family members, favourite book and food, pet or game, and family rules
mcqs.why: A full introduction tells your name, your family members, your favourite book and food, your pet, toy or game, and your family rules.

mcqs.q: The poem sung with actions in this lesson is:

lessons.notes_html:
Gender

Masculine words are for males, feminine words are for females, and neuter words are for things with no male or female gender.

lessons.title: Digraphs, Trigraphs and Spellings
lessons.notes_html:
Syllables

  • treat = treat (1)
  • express = ex-press (2)
  • quote = quote (1)
  • companion = com-pan-ion (3)

Digraphs and Trigraphs

A digraph is two letters making one sound; a trigraph is three letters making one sound.

  • wh (initial) — why, wheat.
  • sh (final) — fish, dish.
  • sch (initial) — schedule, scholar.
  • igh (middle) — light, flight.
  • tch (final) — watch, batch.

Correct Spellings

Believe, Bright, Please, Flight.

mcqs.q: What is a digraph?
mcqs.why: A digraph is two letters making one sound, like wh in why; a trigraph is three letters making one sound.

mcqs.q: Which pair shows the digraph 'wh' at the start?

mcqs.why: Light and flight have the trigraph igh in the middle, which makes one sound.

mcqs.why: Sch is three letters making one sound, so it is a trigraph, found at the start of schedule and scholar.

mcqs.q: Which pair shows 'tch' at the end?

lessons.title: Grammar: Present Continuous and Conjunctions
lessons.notes_html:
Present Continuous Tense

The present continuous tense shows an action happening now. It uses is / am / are + verb-ing.

  • We / You / They are eating, jumping, running.
  • He / She / It is walking, playing, running.
  • I am eating, jumping, running.
  • Present continuous verbs in sentences: are sitting, am looking, is playing, are eating, is walking, are reading.

Conjunctions in a Paragraph

Sameer and his sister were standing outside the gate. They saw their uncle coming towards them. He was holding an umbrella in his hand because it was raining. I asked him if he would like to have tea or coffee. He thanked and went away.

mcqs.q: What does the present continuous tense show?
mcqs.why: The present continuous tense shows an action happening now, using is/am/are + verb-ing.

mcqs.q: Which is the correct form: 'He ______ playing.'
mcqs.why: With he, she or it we use 'is' + verb-ing in the present continuous tense: He is playing.

mcqs.why: With we, you or they we use 'are' + verb-ing: They are eating.

mcqs.q: Which is the correct form: 'I ______ running.'
mcqs.why: With 'I' we always use 'am' in the present continuous tense: I am running.

mcqs.q: Which group takes 'is' in the present continuous tense?
mcqs.why: He, she and it take 'is' + verb-ing, while we, you and they take 'are', and 'I' takes 'am'.

mcqs.why: Are sitting is present continuous (are + verb-ing); the lesson also lists am looking, is playing and are reading.

mcqs.why: The paragraph begins: 'Sameer and his sister were standing outside the gate.'

mcqs.why: Sameer asked him if he would like to have tea or coffee, using the conjunction 'or'.

mcqs.why: The paragraph joins its sentences with and, because and or — all conjunctions.

lessons.title: Story Writing: Elements, 'Hare and Tortoise' and 'A Zoo Elephant'
lessons.notes_html:
Elements of a Story

The elements of a story are: beginning, middle and end; title; characters; place; time.

Model Story: Hare and Tortoise

Once a hare and a tortoise lived in a forest. The hare laughed at the slow tortoise, so they decided to race. In the middle of the race the hare slept under a tree, thinking he would win easily. The tortoise walked slowly but steadily and reached the finish line first.

Moral: Slow and steady wins the race.

Model Story: A Zoo Elephant

Babloo, an elephant from Lahore zoo, likes to eat peanuts and popcorns. He feels happy to get food from children. Children love it for rides. He looks fresh after taking a bath. Babloo is loved by all the children who visit the zoo.

lessons.title: Contractions and Yes/No Answers
lessons.notes_html:
Contractions

A contraction is a short form of two words joined with an apostrophe.

  • I do not — I don't like a banana.
  • We do not — We don't enjoy this game.
  • You do not — You don't run fast.
  • They do not — They don't live in China.
  • He does not — He doesn't play football.
  • She does not — She doesn't go to her village.
  • It does not — It doesn't fly high.

Short Yes/No Answers

  • Do I like a banana? Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
  • Does he play football? Yes, he does. / No, he doesn't.
  • Does it fly high? Yes, it does. / No, it doesn't.

The same pattern is used with we, you, they and she: Yes, we do / No, we don't; Yes, they do / No, they don't; Yes, she does / No, she doesn't.

options: A long form of a word
A short form of two words joined with an apostrophe
mcqs.why: A contraction is a short form of two words joined with an apostrophe, like don't for do not.

mcqs.why: With I, we and you, 'do not' contracts to 'don't': I don't like a banana.

mcqs.why: With he, she and it, 'does not' contracts to 'doesn't': He doesn't play football.

mcqs.q: What is the short answer to 'Do I like a banana?' (yes)
mcqs.why: Questions with 'do' take the short answer 'Yes, I do' or 'No, I don't'.

mcqs.q: What is the short answer to 'Does he play football?' (no)
mcqs.why: Questions with 'does' take the short answer 'Yes, he does' or 'No, he doesn't'.

mcqs.why: With they (and we, you, I), 'do not' becomes 'don't': They don't live in China.

mcqs.why: With 'does' and 'it', the short answers are 'Yes, it does' and 'No, it doesn't'.

mcqs.why: She takes 'does not', which contracts to 'doesn't': She doesn't go to her village.

mcqs.why: We pairs with 'do not' → 'don't', so 'We don't enjoy this game' is correct.

mcqs.why: In a contraction the apostrophe takes the place of the missing letters, like the 'o' of not in don't.

Road Safety Facts

lessons.title: Can and Cannot: Ability
lessons.notes_html:
Can / Cannot

Can shows ability; cannot shows that someone is not able to do something.

  • He cannot jump.
  • It can hop.
  • He can write.
  • He cannot swim.
  • They can sing.
  • She can play.
  • He cannot see.
  • They can fly.

Model: Three things I can do — I can read, write and swim. Three things I cannot do — I cannot fly, drive a car and climb a tall tree.

  • safety = safe-ty (2)
  • cross = cross (1)
  • image = im-age (2)

First squeeze four drops from a lemon. Do the same to an onion. Mix both of the juices with the grains of sugar in an empty dish. Dip a toothpick in the ink. Write your message on a piece of paper. After the ink is dry, iron the paper. You will see the hidden message.

lessons.title: Syllables and Homophones
lessons.notes_html:
Syllables

  • victory = vic-to-ry (3)
  • defeat = de-feat (2)
  • struggle = strug-gle (2)
  • sibling = sib-ling (2)
  • cheerful = cheer-ful (2)
  • interact = in-ter-act (3)

Homophones

Homophones are words that sound the same but have different meanings and spellings.

  • I will write my name. (right / write)
  • She ate a pear for lunch. (pear / pair)
  • The cat won the race. (won / one)
  • She threw the blue ball in the air. (blew / blue)
  • There is an ant in the hole. (aunt / ant)
  • We hear the bell ringing. (here / hear)
  • I see a bee buzzing around. (be / bee)

mcqs.q: How many syllables are there in 'victory'?
mcqs.why: Victory is divided as vic-to-ry, which gives three syllables.

mcqs.q: How many syllables are there in 'defeat'?
mcqs.why: Defeat is divided as de-feat, which gives two syllables.

mcqs.q: What are homophones?
options: Words that sound the same but have different meanings and spellings
mcqs.why: Homophones are words that sound the same but have different meanings and spellings, like right and write.

mcqs.q: 'I will ______ my name.' Choose the correct homophone.
mcqs.why: We write our name with a pen, so 'write' is correct; 'right' means correct.

mcqs.q: 'She ate a ______ for lunch.' Choose the correct homophone.
mcqs.why: A pear is a fruit we can eat for lunch; a pair means two of something.

mcqs.q: 'The cat ______ the race.' Choose the correct homophone.
mcqs.why: Won is the past of win: the cat won the race. 'One' is the number 1.

mcqs.q: 'She threw the ______ ball in the air.' Choose the correct homophone.
mcqs.why: Blue is the colour of the ball; 'blew' is the past of blow.

mcqs.q: 'We ______ the bell ringing.' Choose the correct homophone.
mcqs.why: We hear sounds with our ears; 'here' tells a place.

mcqs.q: How many syllables are there in 'interact'?
mcqs.why: Interact is divided as in-ter-act, which gives three syllables.

mcqs.q: 'There is an ______ in the hole.' Choose the correct homophone.
mcqs.why: An ant is a small insect that can be in a hole; an aunt is a relative.

lessons.title: Word Meanings, Syllables and Correct Spellings

lessons.title: Grammar: Pronouns, Possessive Pronouns, Verbs, and 'do' and 'have'
lessons.notes_html:
Possessive Pronouns

  • My parents and I live in this house. The house is ours.
  • The jacket belongs to Beena. It is hers.
  • I bought a new bike. It is mine.
  • The bag belongs to Amir. The bag is his.

Pronouns in Sentences

The pronouns are: It (It is important for humans); We, us, It (We must switch off the extra lights and fans to save electricity. It will help us saving electricity).

Verbs

The verbs in the sentences are: rises (The sun rises in the east), goes (My brother goes to school on time), are coming (My friends are coming to my birthday party at 5 p.m.), has read (Sameer has read two storybooks), went (We went to watch a movie yesterday).

Do and Have

  • I have a red shirt.
  • He can do his homework at night.
  • Hammad did not have new books.
  • My mother cannot do exercise daily.
  • They have many friends.

mcqs.q: 'My parents and I live in this house. The house is ______.'
mcqs.why: The house belongs to my parents and me, so it is 'ours' — the possessive pronoun for we.

mcqs.q: 'The jacket belongs to Beena. It is ______.'
mcqs.why: The jacket belongs to Beena, a girl, so it is 'hers'.

mcqs.q: 'I bought a new bike. It is ______.'
mcqs.why: The bike belongs to me ('I'), so it is 'mine'.

mcqs.q: 'The bag belongs to Amir. The bag is ______.'
mcqs.why: The bag belongs to Amir, a boy, so the bag is 'his'.

mcqs.q: In 'It is important for humans', the pronoun is:
mcqs.why: It is the pronoun in this sentence, standing in place of a noun.

mcqs.q: Which verbs are in 'The sun rises in the east'?
mcqs.why: Rises is the verb — the action word; sun and east are nouns.

mcqs.q: In 'Sameer has read two storybooks', the verb is:
mcqs.why: Has read is the verb group in this sentence; Sameer is the subject and storybooks are nouns.

mcqs.q: Which sentence uses 'have' correctly?
mcqs.why: With 'I' we use 'have': I have a red shirt.

mcqs.q: 'Hammad did not have new books' — the verb word showing possession is:
mcqs.why: Have shows possession (owning); Hammad did not have — did not own — new books.

mcqs.q: 'They have many friends' — 'have' shows:
mcqs.why: Here 'have' shows possession: the friends belong to them; do and have are the grammar words of this lesson.

lessons.title: Vocabulary, Nouns and Adjectives, Prepositions and Plurals
lessons.notes_html:
Word Meanings and Syllables

  • safety = safe-ty (2) — safe from injury or accident.

rain, game, children, please.

Nouns and Adjectives

  • Nouns: shirt, horse, dish, room, dress.
  • Adjectives: long, black, sweet, clean, nice.

Prepositions

The prepositions are: into (Pour water into the bowl), on (We sit on the chair), under (A cat is under the table), over (The clouds are over the mountains).

'Can' for Ability (Model)

lessons.title: Writing: Verb Forms and a Story

lessons.title: Dictionary Use, 'ed' Sounds and Wh- Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Using a Dictionary

A dictionary is a book which has a list of words and their meanings. It is always in alphabetical order.

Alphabetical order: brush, clean, decay, filthy, tooth, wash.

Word Meanings and Syllables

  • perfect = per-fect (2) — exact, correct in every detail.
  • filthy = fil-thy (2) — dirty.
  • spell = spell (1) — a magic word or formula.
  • decay = de-cay (2) — rotting of teeth.
  • distasteful = dis-taste-ful (3) — bad taste.
  • delight = de-light (2) — great pleasure or happiness.

The 'ed' Sounds

  • /id/ — delighted, decided (also: needed, wanted).
  • /t/ — liked (also: asked, missed).
  • /d/ — tried, enjoyed (also: buzzed, called).

Wh- Questions and Answers (Models)

  • What is this? This is an old camera.
  • When will you go to the zoo? I will go on Sunday.
  • Where is my jacket? It is in my bedroom.
  • Who is your friend? Hammad is my friend.
  • Whom will you invite? I will invite all my classmates.
  • Which colour do you like? I like brown colour.
  • Whose watch is this? This is mine.
  • Why are you so late? I missed the morning bus.
  • How do you feel now? I am much better now.

Making Wh- Questions

  • Ellisa wants to buy a book — Who wants to buy a book?
  • My friend's birthday is on 26th — When is your friend's birthday?
  • It's 10 o'clock — What is the time?
  • My uncle's house is in Satellite Town — Where is your uncle's house?
